title: Chapter 17
content:
Stepping out of the taxi, Jakyeong trudged up the winding hill. Swarms of bugs buzzed in a frenzy around the sickly glow of the streetlamps. Suddenly, a moth the size of an open palm swooped past his ear with a heavy whirring hum. Dignity instantly forgotten, Jakyeong flinched violently, ducking out of the way in pure revulsion.

Though not far from Seoul proper, Kang Il-hyun’s secluded estate sat completely isolated from civil society, like a fortress marooned in the middle of nowhere. Surrounded by dense, shadowy woods, walking the access road alone felt unsettlingly grim. With every step closer to the sprawling mansion, his boots grew heavier.

Parked near the front gate was a pristine white SUV he hadn't seen before. A guest?

Before he could reach the intercom, Park Tae-soo spotted him from the courtyard and sprinted over in a hurry.

"Where on earth have you been? Executive Director Kang has been waiting for you for hours."

"Waiting... for me? Why?"

"Just come inside."

Refusing to elaborate, Tae-soo ushered Jakyeong straight through the front doors.

Slipping into indoor slippers at the entryway, the low hum of conversation drifted from the main hall. Peeking around the corner, Jakyeong caught sight of an unfamiliar figure sitting casually on the living room sofa.

With her hair pulled back into a simple high ponytail, dressed only in a plain white tee and blue jeans, the woman possessed the kind of striking, breathtaking beauty that instantly commanded the room. Even Jakyeong, who had seen his fair share of stunning people across the globe, found himself momentarily frozen.

Spotting him, she rose to her feet and closed the distance with open arms.

"Yi-an! It's so wonderful to meet you."

Before he could take a step back, she wrapped him in a warm, welcoming embrace, patting his back affectionately. The fresh, floral scent of expensive shampoo tickled his nose.

Stepping back, she offered her hand. Jakyeong quickly wiped his right palm against his trousers before taking it. Her fingers were long, elegant, and remarkably soft.

"Welcome to Korea! The last time I saw you, you were just a baby—look how handsome you've become! Isn't he, Il-hyun?"

Il-hyun?

Hearing her use the man's given name so effortlessly, the pieces clicked into place. Kang Yu-jung. Il-hyun's older sister—a trauma surgeon, and the only sibling who shared the same biological mother. He hadn't expected her to be this drop-dead gorgeous.

As Jakyeong stood there staring, his eyes drifted past her shoulder and collided straight with Kang Il-hyun's.

Slouched on the adjacent sofa with an arm draped over the backrest, Il-hyun was eyeing him with a distinctly crooked, cold glare. What's with that venomous look? Annoyed as he was, Jakyeong couldn't afford to break character, so he just smiled innocently.

Yu-jung pulled Jakyeong over by the wrist, guiding him to the sofa.

"Heavens, look how tall you've grown! Do you remember when we met years ago?"

"Ah... no, I'm afraid not..."

"Well, of course not. You were just a toddler. It was during a diplomatic summit in Tokyo—you latched onto our Il-hyun’s pant leg and threw the biggest tantrum!"

"Director Kang mentioned... that he hit me."

"Oh, he told you?" Yu-jung scoffed. "He’s been twisted like that since he was in diapers. As you can see, not a damn thing has changed, so please try to bear with him, Yi-an."

"No, really... he's been very kind to me."

The hollow lie slipped out smoothly, but Yu-jung simply waved a dismissive hand.

"He's my brother, I know him best. Usually, people try to defend their siblings by saying 'he's actually a sweet boy deep down,' but I can't bring myself to tell a lie that big."

She roasted her brother without a shred of hesitation. Jakyeong felt a petty wave of satisfaction wash over him. A subtle smirk twitched at the corner of his lips, but the second his eyes met Il-hyun's icy stare, he wiped the expression off his face instantly.

"If you're done with your business, get going," Il-hyun said flatly. "It's late."

Yu-jung pursed her lips, shooting Jakyeong a look that said See what I mean? But despite her mock pout, she gathered her purse and rose from the sofa without lingering.

She turned to Jakyeong with a bright, luminous smile. "I'll see you tomorrow then!"

Tomorrow? Jakyeong’s eyes widened.

"Father invited you to family dinner," she explained. "Everyone will be there, so just ride over with Director Kang when he leaves."

Jakyeong’s eyes naturally darted back to Il-hyun.

A full family dinner. Would attending give him a chance to deduce which sibling or director put out the contract on Il-hyun's life? The sudden invitation threw him off, but the prospect of meeting the entire suspect pool in one room sparked a flicker of dark curiosity. His dossier pointed toward a few likely candidates, but until he saw them interact in person, it was all speculation.

"Well, I'm off," Yu-jung said, offering a light wave before heading toward the foyer.

Jakyeong considered walking her to the door, but Il-hyun caught his eye, giving a subtle nod toward the empty seat opposite him. Jakyeong walked over and sat down.

The house felt eerily quiet tonight—no guards patrolling the halls, not even the elderly housekeeper in sight. Feeling the suffocating silence, Jakyeong scratched the back of his neck nervously.

"Your sister is extraordinarily beautiful."

"Where were you all evening?" Il-hyun asked, skipping the flattery entirely.

"I was... hanging out with your younger brother..."

"My men reported you weren't with him."

Jakyeong anticipated the report, but having the question fired point-blank still tightened the knot in his stomach.

"I slipped out for a bit to walk around on my own..."

"While miraculously giving both my surveillance guards the slip?"

Jakyeong widened his eyes, putting on a look of total shock. "Guards? What guards? I didn't see anyone. Did you... put a tail on me, Director Kang?"

He deliberately injected a hurt, offended edge into his tone. Right—no matter how terrifying Kang Il-hyun is, Jang Yi-an is an esteemed international VIP. There was no need to crawl on his knees.

Il-hyun stared at him with an unreadable, calculating gaze. Jakyeong didn't look away, meeting the stare head-on.

"Director Kang... I came to Korea for a change of pace. To study art, get some fresh air, and blow off some steam after being cooped up inside all my life. Being kept on a leash like a prisoner is a bit much, don't you think?"

Il-hyun said nothing, his dark pupils boring straight into Jakyeong's. What? Stare all you want, what are you gonna do about it?

Just as Jakyeong pushed back with his eyes, Il-hyun gave a slow, measured nod.

"Fair enough. My oversight. You're a grown man—hardly helpless. I won't restrict your movements around the city. However, you are never to go out alone. Whether it's with Kang Seok-joo or my security personnel, you must move in groups of two or more. As long as you are under this roof, I am your legal guardian. I gave your grandfather my word."

"I'm... hardly a child, though."

"You're not. But if a hair on your head is harmed, the fallout falls entirely on my shoulders. So I'm asking this of you—not for your sake, but for mine. We have an understanding, don't we?"

In other words: don't make a mess for me to clean up.

Sensing that pushing further would only trigger another lecture, Jakyeong nodded submissively. All he wanted was to retreat to his room and collapse.

The moment Il-hyun dismissed him, Jakyeong sprang up from the sofa and bolted toward the stairs. Even as he climbed the spiral steps, he could feel Il-hyun’s heavy gaze tracking him from below.

Reaching the second-floor master suite, he tore open the top buttons of his suffocating shirt and collapsed flat onto the mattress.

Then he froze.

High above, the dome of the security camera was still blinking right at him.

Jakyeong sat bolt upright, scowling in disbelief. The bastard said out of his own mouth he’d have it removed today.

Marching back down to the ground floor, Il-hyun was no longer in the living room. Jakyeong navigated the dim corridor toward the master bedroom at the end of the wing. With every step, a daring thought took root in his mind.

He knew where Il-hyun slept, but he’d never once set foot inside the master quarters. This might be the perfect chance to scout the layout.

Licking his lower lip, he stopped outside the heavy door and gave two crisp knocks. Silence. Just as he raised his knuckles for a second attempt, the door unlatched with a quiet click.

Kang Il-hyun stood in the doorway, still dressed in his crisp dress shirt, completely unruffled. Does this psycho sleep in full business attire?

Il-hyun’s eyes drifted down from Jakyeong’s face, lingering on the open collar of his unbuttoned shirt.

"Is something the matter?"

"I have something to discuss... May I come in for a moment?"

"Go ahead."

Il-hyun stepped aside, granting entrance without hesitation. Inside, Jakyeong silently celebrated.

The master suite featured an expansive private parlor, nearly identical in architecture to the guest suite upstairs, though the ambiance was noticeably darker and more austere. Dominating an entire wall was a massive recessed aquarium where two sleek reef sharks glided silently through the blue water.

Taking the seat Il-hyun gestured to, Jakyeong’s eyes swept the room, mapping out every corner.

"Would you like some tea?"

"Ah, no thank you."

"A drink, then?"

"I can't really hold my liquor..."

"Pity."

Sitting face-to-face in a soundproof room was excruciatingly awkward. Jakyeong fought with everything he had to banish the humiliating memory from the basement vault two nights ago.

"You said you had something to discuss. Go on."

"You promised you would have the camera removed from my bedroom today... but it's still there."

"Is it?" Il-hyun asked, pulling an innocent, clueless expression that insulted Jakyeong's intelligence. There was zero chance the staff had failed to carry out an explicit order.

"Is there really a pressing need to take it down?" Il-hyun murmured smoothly.

Jakyeong bit his inner cheek. He’d explained this a dozen times, and Il-hyun had brought it up himself just yesterday morning. Keeping his temper under lock and key, Jakyeong offered a meek, polite smile.

"Are you... doing this on purpose?"

"Doing what?"

"Tormenting me..."

"Do I strike you as a psychopath who harasses guests for sport?"

Jakyeong’s lips parted, barely swallowing his rage, but his tone sharpened despite his best efforts. "Then why leave it up? Put yourself in my shoes, Director Kang. Would you enjoy sleeping knowing someone is watching your every move?"

"I wouldn't care."

"Well, I sleep completely naked. It's the only way I can rest comfortably. Ever since I arrived, I haven't gotten a single night of decent sleep."

"Then sleep naked," Il-hyun said flatly.

"..."

"Make yourself at home."

Jakyeong’s breath hitched in his throat. In his mind, he was already slamming both fists onto the mahogany table and shattering the bastard's jaw. Does this prick actually have a thing for me? Was the 'protection' line just an excuse to watch me strip? Was that little handshake at the airport just a cheap come-on?

The mounting disgust twisted Jakyeong's expression into something genuinely foul.

"Director Kang."

The sharp bite in Jakyeong's voice was impossible to hide, but Il-hyun merely chuckled, his demeanor unfazed.

"My apologies. Wipe that scowl off your face. The crew had an emergency today and had to reschedule, but the camera will be dismantled tomorrow. I was just teasing—you look amusing when you get flustered."

You arrogant piece of shit.

"And besides..." Il-hyun paused, trailing off.

I swear to God, I can never read this bastard.

"...I was genuinely curious."

Il-hyun reached for the heavy silver cigarette case on the table, sliding an obsidian ashtray toward himself. Popping the latch, he selected a smoke.

"Curious about what?" Jakyeong asked, his tone still bristling.

Placing the cigarette between his lips, Il-hyun answered with terrifying, offhand ease.

"Why a frail, delicate young master has a full tattoo across his shoulder."

"..."

The air in the room died. The brown irises behind Jakyeong’s horn-rimmed glasses violently dilated.

"And why someone who speaks with such polite deference... has the dead, predatory eyes of an underworld thug."

"..."

Holding the unlit cigarette between his teeth, Kang Il-hyun curved his lips into a slow, chilling grin.

"I've been dying to find out."

Jakyeong’s breath locked in his chest. His hands clenched into white-knuckled fists against his knees, his throat going bone-dry as a wave of icy sweat drenched his spine.

Just as the red alarm flared at maximum volume inside his skull, Il-hyun flicked his lighter.

Fsshh.

A blue flame danced for a fleeting heartbeat before vanishing, replaced by a dense cloud of pale gray smoke billowing between them.

Watching Jakyeong glare rigidly through the haze, a look of pure, fascinated amusement lit up Il-hyun’s eyes.

"Well, look at that. Don't tell me you smoke, too?"
